items.headline: Kyler Murray named Vikings starting QB over J.J. McCarthy
items.summary: Kevin O'Connell ended Minnesota's training-camp battle, giving the former No. 1 overall pick the Week 1 start against Green Bay. Murray, signed to a one-year deal in March after his Arizona release, gets the same career-reset shot Sam Darnold parlayed into a long-term Seahawks deal. McCarthy's future — and his 2028 fifth-year option — is now in doubt.

items.headline: Jets CB Stiggers hospitalized after collapsing at practice
items.summary: New York Jets cornerback Stiggers was taken to a hospital after collapsing during practice, the scariest moment of camp season. The team has not yet released details on his condition.

items.headline: Chiefs' Rashee Rice calls jail sentence a 'learning experience'
items.summary: Speaking at Chiefs camp, wide receiver Rashee Rice addressed his jail sentence publicly, framing it as a learning experience as he works back toward the field for Kansas City.

items.headline: Red Sox land C Adley Rutschman from Orioles in deadline blockbuster
items.summary: Boston's biggest deadline swing in years: a 5-for-2 deal sending Kyson Witherspoon (their 2025 first-rounder), catcher Carlos Narváez, Eyanson, Azocar and a PTBNL to Baltimore for the All-Star switch-hitting catcher and backup Jake Rogers. The Sox also stunned the league by dealing shortstop Marcelo Mayer to San Francisco for reliever Erik Miller, and added outfielder Eli White from Atlanta.

items.headline: Michael Brennan wins Wyndham, vaults into FedExCup Playoffs
items.summary: Brennan made five straight birdies Sunday and closed with a 6-under 64 to win the Wyndham Championship by three over Beau Hossler, jumping from No. 105 to No. 47 in the FedExCup. Jackson Koivun held the No. 70 bubble spot — matching Tiger Woods' record for fewest starts (five) needed to reach the postseason. The playoffs open Aug. 13 at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis.

items.headline: Dodgers snap seven-game skid, beat Diamondbacks in 10
items.summary: Los Angeles finally stopped the bleeding, edging Arizona in 10 innings to end a seven-game losing streak that had tightened the NL West race.

items.headline: Ty Gibbs holds on to win NASCAR Cup Series race in Iowa
items.summary: Ty Gibbs survived the late laps at Iowa Speedway to take the Cup Series checkered flag, a key win as the playoff picture takes shape.

items.headline: Arsenal signs Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle for £75M
items.summary: The Premier League champions landed the 28-year-old Brazil midfielder — Newcastle's former captain — on a four-year deal (plus an option year) worth a reported £75M ($101M). Guimarães, who called it one of the toughest decisions of his life, joins Declan Rice in Arsenal's midfield as the club opens its title defense.

items.headline: Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrines 2026 class: Brees, Fitzgerald
items.summary: Drew Brees and Larry Fitzgerald headlined the 2026 class formally enshrined in Canton. Arizona also announced it will retire Fitzgerald's No. 11.

items.headline: NY Liberty win WNBA Commissioner's Cup, first two-time champion
items.summary: New York defeated the Las Vegas Aces 93-85 to take the 2026 Commissioner's Cup, becoming the first franchise to win the in-season tournament twice.

items.headline: NFL camps open: Hurts' speed drawing raves, injuries hit contenders
items.summary: All 32 teams are in training camp ahead of the Sept. 13 openers. Jalen Hurts' added speed is the talk of Eagles camp; the Saints could lose Cam Jordan (hamstring) for the start of the season; Ravens CB Nate Wiggins went down in 1-on-1 drills; Green Bay's Greenard (pec) is out a couple more weeks.

items.headline: Spain wins 2026 World Cup, beating Messi's Argentina 1-0 in extra time
items.summary: Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner off a Nico Williams knockdown ended Argentina's reign in the New York-New Jersey final and spoiled Messi's last World Cup match. Spain conceded just one goal in eight games — a record for a champion — and became the first nation to hold the men's and women's titles simultaneously. Luis de la Fuente, 65, is the oldest coach to win it; Mbappé took the Golden Boot. The 48-team, 104-match tournament across the USA, Canada and Mexico was the biggest ever.
